small_guidance:
- The conv3d dominates runtime now (fast_p ~0.53 with GN+min+clamp already fused). Tuning BLOCK_S/num_warps on the GN kernel will not close the gap; only marginal gains (e.g. BLOCK_S=8192, num_warps=4 since per-group S=14*62*62 ≈ 53k) are possible.
- Try a single-pass Welford for GN to halve global loads on the normalization tail, and absorb min/clamp into a single `tl.clamp(x, min_value, min(min_value, max_value))` (since min then clamp[min_value,max_value] always returns ≤min_value, so the effective output is clamp(x, min_value, min_value) = min_value when x≥min_value, else clamp to [min_value,...] — verify and simplify).
- Skip the dropout module call at eval and keep training-mode path; the F.dropout launch is non-trivial relative to the fused kernel.
large_guidance:
- Replace `nn.Conv3d` with a custom Triton im2col-style GEMM kernel: one program per (N, OC-tile, output-spatial tile), implicit im2col gather of the 3×3×3 patch over IC=3 (K = 3*27 = 81, very small). With OC=16, this is a skinny GEMM — use BLOCK_M=16 (OC), BLOCK_N=64-128 (spatial), BLOCK_K=81 fully unrolled.
- Fuse the GroupNorm reduction's first pass into the conv epilogue by writing per-(N,G) partial sum/sum_sq into a small scratch buffer alongside the conv output, so pass-2 of GN only needs one read instead of two. Alternatively, since OC=16 and groups=8 (CPG=2), make the conv kernel emit a whole group's worth of channels per program and do GN entirely in-register without a separate kernel.
- Channels-last (NDHWC) layout for the conv output makes the GN reduction over (C-per-group, S) coalesced when CPG is the inner stride; consider laying out as (N, G, CPG, S) directly from the conv epilogue.
